title.en: A Man in White Asks About Islam, Faith, and the Hour
title.zh: 白衣人問：伊斯蘭、信仰與末日

region.en: Medina, among the seated Companions (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那眾聖門弟子之間（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari (d. 870), Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50 — the Hadith of Jibril, narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man with intensely white clothes and intensely black hair, with no trace of journey, comes and sits knee to knee before the Prophet and asks: What is Islam? What is faith? What is excellence (ihsan)? When will the Hour come? The Prophet answers each in turn; the questioner affirms and vanishes. 'That was Jibril, come to teach you your religion.'
summary.zh: 一白衣黑髮之人前來，衣服極白、頭髮極黑，不見旅塵。他與先知膝對膝而坐，問：何為伊斯蘭？何為信仰？何為至善？末日何時？先知逐一作答；問者認可而離去。『那是吉布里勒，來教你們你們的宗教。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original for comparative study, not a religious claim.

passages.text: While we were sitting with the Messenger of God one day, a man came whose clothes were intensely white and whose hair was intensely black; no sign of travel could be seen on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down close to the Prophet, rested his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs, and said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.' The Prophet said: 'Islam is that you testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, that you keep up the prayer, pay the poor-due, fast Ramadan, and make the pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way.' The man said, 'You have spoken truly.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.

passages.text: We were amazed that he asked and confirmed him. Then he said: 'Tell me about faith.' He said: 'That you believe in God, and His angels, and His Books, and His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in the decree, its good and its evil.' He said, 'You have spoken truly. Then tell me about excellence.' He said: 'That you worship God as if you saw Him, for if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.' He said, 'You have spoken truly. Then tell me about the Hour.' He said: 'The one questioned knows no more than the questioner.' He said, 'Then tell me about its signs.' He said: 'That the slave-girl shall give birth to her mistress, and that you will see barefoot, naked, destitute shepherds competing in building tall structures.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.

passages.text: Then he went away, and I stayed some while. Then he said: 'O Umar, do you know who the questioner was?' I said, 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'That was Jibril, who came to you to teach you your religion.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman, no. 50; not verbatim.

title.en: Three Men and the Rock: Each Calls on His Best Deed
title.zh: 三人與磐石：各以其善行求主

region.en: Mountain cave on a journey (symbolic pin)

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272 — narrated by Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Three men take shelter in a cave; a boulder rolls down and seals the entrance. None can be released except by prayer for his best deed: the first for his duty to his parents; the second for resisting temptation for God's sake; the third for paying a labourer whose wages grew like the earth's increase. Each prayer moves the rock a little, until they come out walking in the sunlight.
summary.zh: 三人避雨入洞；巨石滾落封住洞口。除非各以一生最佳善行祈求，否則無法出洞：第一人為孝敬父母而求；第二人為敬畏主而守戒；第三人為償還長大如土之息的工錢而求。每次祈禱石移一寸，直至三人在陽光中走出。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Three men were travelling and were overtaken by rain; they came to a mountain and took shelter in a cave, and a boulder of the mountain rolled down and shut them in. They said to one another, 'Nothing can deliver you from this rock but that you pray to God with some righteous deed that belongs to each of you.' One said: 'O God, I had aged parents, and I never gave my children or my wealth drink before them; I rose one night with milk for them and stood by their heads while they slept — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us from this rock.' It moved a hand's breadth from the mouth of the cave.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; not verbatim.

passages.text: The second said: 'O God, I loved my cousin as deeply as a man can love a woman, and she refused me save for a great sum of money. I laboured until I gathered it, and when I sat between her thighs she said, Fear God, and do not break the seal except lawfully; and I left her, though she was the dearest of all people to me — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us.' It moved two hands' breadths. The third said: 'O God, I hired labourers and paid all but one who went away; I sowed his wage, and it grew into wealth of cattle and sheep and wealth. Then he came and said, O servant of God, pay me my wage; and I pointed to the cattle and sheep and camels: take them all. He thought I mocked him, but I gave him the whole — if I did that seeking Thy face, relieve us.' The rock moved from the mouth of the cave, and they came out walking in the sunlight.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2272; not verbatim.

title.en: The Woman Punished for a Cat

region.en: Hereafter visions told in Medina (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那所講的後世異象（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Anbiya, no. 3318 (also Kitab al-Ashriba); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3318 — narrated by Ibn Umar

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet passes by a woman among the punished of the Hereafter who is holding a cat, keeping it captive, neither feeding it nor letting it eat the vermin of the earth until it dies of hunger. The Prophet is asked whether it is one of the jinn; he answers that it is one of the beings punished for imprisoning a cat — a creature that God had allowed to roam and that she failed to feed or free.
summary.zh: 先知見後世受罰者中一女子，手抱一貓，拘禁之，不餵食，也不放其食地上之蟲，直至餓死。人問：是精靈嗎？先知答：是被懲罰的生靈之一——她拘禁真主所任其自由行走之貓，不餵不縱。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God passed by a woman who was among the punished of the Hereafter, holding a cat she had tethered. She had neither fed it nor given it water to drink, nor had she freed it to eat the creeping things of the earth, until it died of hunger. He was asked whether it was one of the jinn, and he said that it was one of the jinn? He said, 'It was not a jinni: it was a woman among the punished, punished for a cat she had kept captive — she neither fed it nor gave it drink, nor freed it to eat the creatures of the earth, till it died.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3318; not verbatim.

title.en: A Dog Licking the Sand: Water for a Thirsty Creature
title.zh: 舔沙之犬：給乾渴生靈一口水

region.zh: 井間沙漠道（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Musaqat, no. 2363 (variant: Sahih Muslim); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: A man on a journey finds a well, descends and drinks, and comes out to see a panting dog licking the moist sand for water. The man takes his shoe, fills it with water, and gives the dog to drink; God thanks him and forgives him. The Companions ask whether there is reward even in beasts — 'There is a reward in every living creature.' A sinful woman of the Israelites is told of in the same telling, forgiven for giving water to a dog.
summary.zh: 一人行路遇井，下井飲水，出井見一犬喘息舔沙覓水。此人以鞋盛水飲犬；主感謝他並赦之。聖門弟子問：畜生也有回賜嗎？——『凡有生命之物皆有回賜。』同傳說以色列人一罪婦，因飲犬水而被赦。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: While a man was walking on a road he became very thirsty, and found a well; he descended into it and drank and came out, and there was a dog panting and licking the moist earth for water. The man said to himself, This dog is as thirsty as I was; so he went down into the well, filled his shoe with water, held it in his mouth, climbed out, and gave the dog to drink. God thanked him for that and forgave him. They said, 'O Messenger of God, is there a reward for us in the animals?' He said: 'In every living creature there is a reward.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363; not verbatim.

passages.text: A prostitute among the Israelites was forgiven in the same manner: she saw a dog going round a well, about to die of thirst, drew water in her shoe and gave it to drink; and God forgave her for it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2363 (variant narrations); not verbatim.

title.en: The Last of the People of Hell

region.en: Medina, teaching among the Companions (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那聖門弟子中的教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571 — narrated by Ibn Mas'ud

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The last man to leave the Fire will be brought out on hands and knees, and God will say to him: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He comes and finds it full of people and provision: 'My Lord, I find it full of people and provisions.' 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, with the kingdom of a king of the kings of the world?' 'I would be content, my Lord.' Then God laughs, and the man enters — and finds rivers flowing, food bearing fruit, every conceivable provision. He asks for a door and is given one; he goes out, and is told: 'You have been in captivity and then died; enter into the blessing of Paradise forever.'
summary.zh: 火獄居民之最後者，四足爬行而出。主對他說：『去，入樂園吧。』他見樂園滿是人與供給：『主啊，我見其中滿是人與供給。』『亞當的子孫啊，你若得一王中之王的國度可滿足嗎？』——『可滿足，我的主。』主便笑；他入園，見河川流動、果實、各種供給；他求一門而得之，出而復返；告之：『你曾被囚禁而後死去；你將永居樂園之福。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; eschatological imagery kept as spoken in the text.

passages.text: Among the people of Hell there will be he who is the last of them to leave it and the last to enter Paradise; he will come out of the Fire crawling, and God will say to him, 'Go, and enter Paradise.' So he goes and comes to it and finds that it is full of people. He says, 'O Lord, I find it full of people and provision.' God will say to him, 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, if you had the kingdom of a king of the kings of the world?' He will say, 'I would be content, my Lord.' God will say to him, 'Would you be content, O son of Adam, if I gave you the like of the world and as much again?' He will say, 'Yes.' God will laugh at him and say, 'You will have the like of it and ten times as much.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571; not verbatim.

passages.text: The last man of the people of Hell will be the last of his people to leave the Fire, and the last to enter Paradise; God will say to him, 'O son of Adam, if you had the world and as much again, would you be content?' He will say, 'Yes, my Lord.' Then God will say, 'You ask for less than what I have prepared for you.' Then he enters, and finds rivers flowing and trees bearing fruit, and food, and all sorts of provision. He will ask, 'O Lord, may I enter? I have seen all these things.' He will be told: 'You are not one of those who are shut out.' He goes out and comes back to the door and is told, 'Enter — the Fire has been behind you, and Paradise is before you.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6571 (variant narration); not verbatim.

title.en: The Poorest of the People of Paradise

region.zh: 麥地那末世教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572 — narrated by Ibn Mas'ud

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The last of the people of Paradise to enter will be a man whom God allows to enter from outside the gate: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He goes, and thinks it is full; he returns: 'My Lord, I found it full.' Then God says: 'Enter Paradise, and you will have the like of the world and ten times more (or ten times like it).' The man says: 'Are you mocking me, or are You laughing at me, O Lord, though You are the King?' — and God laughs. The man then enters Paradise, and whoever of the people of Paradise was under his rule is placed under his power: even the two women of the jinn, who lie on a carpet with him.
summary.zh: 樂園居民之最後入者，自門外被准進入：『去入樂園。』他以為滿了；他返：『主啊，我見其滿。』主說：『入吧，得與世界同等且十倍（或謂十倍於此）。』那人說：『主啊，你在嘲弄我嗎？你是君王啊。』主便笑。他入園，凡樂園中曾居其下者皆歸其治：即精靈中的兩女，與他同臥一毯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: Among the people of Paradise there will be the last of them to enter it, a man whom God will cause to enter Paradise from outside of the Gate. He will be told, 'Go and enter Paradise.' So he will go and come to it, and think that it is full. He will go back and say, 'O Lord, I found it full.' God will say, 'Go and enter Paradise, for you will have the like of the world and ten times like it.' The man will say, 'Are You mocking me — or are You laughing at me, O Lord, though You are the King?' He will say, 'I am not mocking you, but I am able to do whatever I will.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; not verbatim.

passages.text: When he passes the first of the gates of Paradise, he will say, 'O Lord, how great is this!' He will be told, 'This is for you.' He will find what his soul desires and what pleases his eye, and there will be with him two wives from the houris, each of whom will be wearing seventy rows of garments, and the marrow of their shins will be visible through them from the beauty of their faces. Then when he reaches his dwelling he will find rivers flowing beneath it, and wherever he will go there will be rivers.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, no. 6572; not verbatim.

title.en: Seven Whom God Will Shade on the Day Without Shade
title.zh: 無蔭之日蒙主蔭庇的七種人

region.zh: 麥地那主麻講道（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adhan, no. 660 (variant: no. 1423); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 660 — narrated by Abu Hurayrah

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Seven people will be shaded by God on the day when there is no shade but His shade: a just ruler; a youth who grew up in the worship of God; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who love one another for God, meeting and parting upon that love; a man whom a woman of beauty and position calls to sin, and he answers, 'I fear God'; a man who gives in charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gave; a man who remembers God alone and weeps.
summary.zh: 無蔭之日，主將為七種人設蔭：公道的官長；自幼崇拜主的青年；心繫清真寺者；為主相愛、聚散皆因此愛的兩人；被貌美有勢之女子勾引而答『我懼主』者；施捨隱蔽、左手不知右手所施者；獨處時紀念主而流淚者。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: Seven are the people whom God will shade with His shade on the day when there is no shade but His shade: a just ruler; a young man who has been brought up in the worship of God; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques when he leaves them until he returns to them; two men who love one another for God's sake, who come together upon that love and part upon it; a man who is called by a woman of rank and beauty for sin, and he says, 'I fear God'; a man who gives in charity and hides it, so much so that his left hand does not know what his right hand has given; and a man who remembers God in solitude and his eyes overflow.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 660; not verbatim.

title.en: The Truthful Merchant With the Prophets
title.zh: 與先知同列的誠實商人

region.zh: 麥地那集市教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076 — narrated by Abu Sa'id

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs. Trading must be free of cheating: whoever deceives in buying and selling is not of the honest; whoever takes falsely is not of the truthful. The Prophet forbade the seller to raise the price and the buyer to lower it at the expense of another, and forbade the intermarriage of the tribes in the days of ignorance. 'The buyer and seller have the choice as long as they have not separated; if they speak truth and make clear, their transaction will be blessed; but if they conceal and lie, the blessing is erased.'
summary.zh: 誠實可靠的商人將與先知、誠實者、烈士同列。買賣不可欺詐：欺人者非誠實者，妄取者非誠實者。先知禁止抬高市價、以損人利己之價壓低；『買賣雙方只要未分開，皆可自由選擇；若誠實明言，其交易蒙福；若隱匿撒謊，福分被抹去。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs. And the buyer and the seller have the option of the transaction as long as they have not separated; if both of them speak the truth and make it plain, their transaction will be blessed; but if they speak falsehood and conceal anything, then the blessing of their transaction will be erased.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Buyu', no. 2076; not verbatim.

title.en: The Dinar, the Donkey, and the Neighbor

region.en: Medina, teaching on mutual rights (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 麥地那相互權利教導（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018 (variant: Sahih Muslim); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018 — narrated by Ibn Umar? (traditional attribution: Abu Hurayrah / Ibn Umar narrations)

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: Whosoever believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor; he should offer hospitality; and he should speak good or keep silent. He whose neighbors are not safe from his wrongdoing is not a believer; and no one is safe from the creditor's claims — the dinar, the dirham, the garment, the donkey, the slave — whose owner may ask repayment of any of them. Even a meal may be asked for on behalf of a hungry guest.
summary.zh: 凡信主與末日者，勿傷其鄰；應待客；言善或默然。鄰居不因其惡行而得安寧者非信士；無人能擔保債權不至——金幣、銀幣、衣裳、驢、僕——其主皆可索取。即便是飢餓客人的食膳，也可代為請求。

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Messenger of God said: He who believes in God and the Last Day should not harm his neighbour; and he who believes in God and the Last Day should honour his guest; and he who believes in God and the Last Day should speak good or keep silent. And no one is safe from the claims of debts — the debt of the dinar, or of the dirham, or of the garment, or of the donkey, or of the camel — unless he is a man who would ask for the repayment of his debts; but if the guest comes hungry, then the householder should feed him.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Adab, no. 6018; not verbatim.

title.en: The Camel That Complained to the Prophet

region.zh: 麥地那郊外（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466 (variant narrations); English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466 — narrated by Anas ibn Malik

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet enters the garden of a man of the Ansar; there is a camel. When it sees the Prophet it groans and its eyes flow with tears; the Prophet goes to it and wipes the place of its tears, and it becomes quiet. 'Who is the owner of this camel? Whose camel is this?' A man of the Ansar says, 'It is mine.' The Prophet says: 'Do you not fear God with regard to this beast which He has put in your possession? It complained to me that you keep it hungry and load it heavily.'
summary.zh: 先知入輔士之園；見一駱駝。駱駝見先知則呻吟，眼含淚；先知至其旁拭其淚，駱駝安靜。『這駱駝的主人是誰？』一輔士答：『是我的。』先知說：『你豈不敬畏主——他賜你此獸？它向我訴苦：你餓它且重負之。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original; animal sentience here is a doctrinal claim within the tradition, presented as text.

passages.text: The Prophet once went into the garden of a man of the Ansar, and there was a camel there. When the Prophet came near it, the camel groaned and its eyes flowed with tears. The Prophet came to it and wiped the place of its tears with his hand, and it became quiet. He said, 'Who is the owner of this camel? Whose camel is this?' A man of the Ansar said, 'It is mine, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Do you not fear God concerning this beast which He has given you to possess? It has complained to me that you keep it hungry and load it beyond its strength.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Ahkam, no. 2466; not verbatim.

title.en: Bilal's Call to Prayer After Death

region.zh: 麥加天房庭院（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Recorded 9th century CE in Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014; English paraphrase original

source.work: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014 — the Prophet's dream, narrated by Ibn Umar

texts.license: Arabic original public domain (9th century CE); original English paraphrase

summary.en: The Prophet dreams that he is at the Kaaba, with a man going around it, and another man walking beside him. He asks who they are and is answered: the tall man with red skin and ivory teeth is Ibrahim (Abraham), and the one walking beside him — who looks like Bilal — is the muezzin of Paradise. Waking, the Prophet says: 'This is Bilal, and the tall man is Ibrahim: I have seen the adhan of Paradise and its muezzin.'
summary.zh: 先知夢中在天房處，見一人繞行，另一人與之同行。他問此二人為誰，答曰：高大紅膚、牙如象牙者是易卜拉欣；與之同行者貌似比拉勒——是樂園的宣禮員。醒後先知說：『這是比拉勒，高大者是易卜拉欣：我已見樂園的宣禮及其宣禮員。』

sensitivity.note: Canonical hadith of a living tradition; presented as a paraphrase of the Arabic original.

passages.text: The Prophet said: While I was sleeping I saw myself at the Kaaba, and there was a man beside it going around it. He was tall, with a dark-red complexion, wavy hair, and his two shoulders were like those of a prince; his teeth were like those of a fine ivory comb. Beside him was another man with curly hair and blind in the right eye, resembling Ibn Qatan. The first was walking around the Kaaba, and the other beside him. I asked, 'Who is this man?' It was said, 'He is Ibrahim.' I said, 'And who is the man with him?' It was said, 'He is the Mu'addhin (caller to prayer) of Paradise.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014; not verbatim.

passages.text: The Prophet said: 'I saw in a dream that I was at the Kaaba and saw the one who used to walk beside Bilal.' Then Bilal's call to prayer was heard, and the Prophet said, 'I have seen the Mu'addhin of Paradise, and I have heard the adhan from Bilal who has died.'
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Fitan, no. 7014 (variant narration of the same dream-cycle); not verbatim.
